    Documentation/ HEPkit

    ParticleSelector

    class ParticleSelector

    A model-independent way to identify an external particle.

    Selectors may use a UFO particle name or a signed PDG code, making process definitions convenient while deferring validation to a concrete model.

    Examples

    from symbolica.community import hepkit as hep
electron = hep.ParticleSelector.by_pdg(11)
positron = hep.ParticleSelector.by_name("e+")

    Attributes

    Name Description
    is_name Report whether this selector identifies a particle by name.
    is_pdg Report whether this selector identifies a particle by PDG code.
    name Return the selected particle name
    pdg Return the selected PDG code

    is_name

    ParticleSelector.is_name: builtins.bool

    Report whether this selector identifies a particle by name.

    Examples

    Using the setup in the ParticleSelector class example:

    assert hep.ParticleSelector.by_name("e-").is_name

    is_pdg

    ParticleSelector.is_pdg: builtins.bool

    Report whether this selector identifies a particle by PDG code.

    Examples

    Using the setup in the ParticleSelector class example:

    assert hep.ParticleSelector.by_pdg(11).is_pdg

    name

    ParticleSelector.name: builtins.str

    Return the selected particle name.

    Raises TypeError for a PDG selector. Use is_name to distinguish the selector variants before accessing their payloads.

    Examples

    Using the setup in the ParticleSelector class example:

    assert hep.ParticleSelector.by_name("e-").name == "e-"

    pdg

    ParticleSelector.pdg: builtins.int

    Return the selected PDG code.

    Raises TypeError for a name selector. Use is_pdg to distinguish the selector variants before accessing their payloads.

    Examples

    Using the setup in the ParticleSelector class example:

    assert hep.ParticleSelector.by_pdg(11).pdg == 11

    __eq__

    ParticleSelector.__eq__(other: typing.Any) -> builtins.bool

    Compare with another selector, a particle name, or a PDG code.

    Using the setup in the ParticleSelector class example:

True

    Parameters

    • other (object) Selector, particle-name string, or integer PDG code to compare with.

    __repr__

    ParticleSelector.__repr__() -> builtins.str

    Return a constructor-style representation of the selector.

    Examples

    Using the setup in the ParticleSelector class example:

    __str__

    ParticleSelector.__str__() -> builtins.str

    Format the selector as its particle name or signed PDG code.

    Examples

    Using the setup in the ParticleSelector class example:

    str(hep.ParticleSelector.by_pdg(11))
'11'

    by_name

    ParticleSelector.by_name(name: builtins.str) -> ParticleSelector

    Select a particle by its model name.

    Examples

    Using the setup in the ParticleSelector class example:

    hep.ParticleSelector.by_name("e-").name
'e-'

    Parameters

    • name (str) Particle name as it appears in the model.

    by_pdg

    ParticleSelector.by_pdg(pdg: builtins.int) -> ParticleSelector

    Select a particle by its signed PDG code.

    Examples

    Parameters

    • pdg (int) Signed PDG code of the particle.
